Chapter 4: Clarifying Values and Aligning with the Right Environment
Let’s talk about something that’s just as important as knowing your strengths or your work style—your personal values.
These values act like a compass. They guide your decisions, shape what matters most to you, and help define what you see as acceptable—or not.
When your values line up with your work environment, you’ll notice your motivation and satisfaction soar. But if there’s a gap between what you care about and what your workplace stands for, even the best performers can feel stuck or unfulfilled.
Clarifying your values takes some real, honest reflection. You’ll want to ask yourself: What truly matters to me? What are my non-negotiables? And what kind of legacy do I want to leave behind?
These questions aren’t always easy, and your answers might shift as you gain new experiences or see the world from a fresh perspective.
Here are a few questions that can help bring your values into focus:
What principles guide your choices, especially when things get tough?
Are there lines you just won’t cross, even if it means missing out on a promotion or recognition?
And, what kind of impact do you want your work to have?
Once you’re clear about your values, the next step is to look at your current work environment. Does it support what you believe in?
This isn’t just about the company’s official mission statement—it’s also about the day-to-day culture, the little unwritten rules, and even how people treat each other.
If there’s a disconnect, you might start feeling that internal tug-of-war—a little bit of stress, some frustration, or maybe even total disengagement.
Take this for example: Imagine you value transparency and open communication. But your organization keeps things tightly under wraps. Or maybe you’re someone who thrives on innovation and a bit of risk-taking, but you’re working in a place that sticks strictly to the rules and doesn’t welcome new ideas.
Recognizing these mismatches early on is key.
So, what can you do if your values and your workplace just aren’t lining up?
Well, first, you might look for roles or companies that share your core beliefs. Or, if you’re in a position to influence change, you could advocate for a shift in culture or practice.
But sometimes, if there’s just no way to bridge that gap, it might be time to consider moving on—to protect your own integrity and well-being.
Remember, your values also help you set priorities and make tough choices. When you’re facing competing demands or even ethical dilemmas, being clear about what matters most gives you a steady compass.
This kind of clarity cuts down on stress and boosts your confidence, because you’re acting from a place of conviction, not just following the crowd.
And, just a quick reminder—your values aren’t set in stone. As life changes, so might what’s most important to you.
That’s why it’s so valuable to check in with yourself regularly. Make sure your actions keep lining up with what you care about, so your work stays meaningful and fulfilling along the way.
